COMMON ORAL JUDGMENT 1.
All these appeals involve common questions on law and facts and therefore, they are disposed of by this common judgment treating the First Appeal No. 2675 of 2012 as lead matter.

2. Present appeals are fled by the appellants - original claimants under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter be referred to as "the Act") read with Section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure Code, 1908 challenging the common judgement and award dated 30.12.2010 passed by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge, Surendranagar (hereinafter be referred to as "the Reference Court") in Land Acquisition Reference Nos. 306 of 2001, 307 of 2001, 310 of 2001, 311 of Nagarbhai Gangarambhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24694751/
2 2001, 312 of 2001, 313 of 2001, 314 of 2001, 315 of 2001, 317 of 2001, 318 of 2001, 319 of 2001 &
322 of 2001 respectively, whereby, the Reference Court has awarded Rs.30/- per square meter for non-irrigated lands and Rs.45/- per square meter for irrigated lands, over-and-above the amount awarded by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.

sentences.text: 3. In view of the fact that First Appeal No. 2675 of 2012 is treated as lead matter, facts mentioned in the said First Appeal are considered.

It is the case of the appellant that for the public purpose of Saurashtra Branch Canal of Narmada Yojna, the State Government acquired the lands of the appellant - original claimant situated at NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2675/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/10/2025 undefined Village: Malod, Taluka: Wadhwan, District: Surendranagar.

That,
notification under Section 4(1) of the Act was issued on 20.06.1996 and thereafter, declaration under Section 6 of the Act was published and ultimately, the Special Land Acquisition Officer declared the award on 23.12.1998 and awarded compensation at the rate of Rs.1.50ps. per square meter for non-irrigated lands and Rs.2.25ps. per square meter for irrigated lands in LAQ Case No.
264 of 1996.

4. Being aggrieved, the appellants - original claimants, preferred the aforesaid LAR Cases under Section 18 of the Act for additional compensation of Rs.15/- per square meter for non-irrigated lands and Rs.22.50ps. per square meter for irrigated lands.
That, the respondents had filed their written statements denying all the allegations made in the References.
That, after considering the pleadings of both the sides, the Reference Court had framed the issues at Exh.-12 referred in para-9 and the same were answered in para-10.

After considering the documentary as well as the oral evidence referred in paras-5, 6 and 7 led before the Reference Court, the judgment and award dated 30.12.2010 came to be passed by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge, Surendranagar as aforesaid.
This has aggrieved the appellants, have preferred the present appeals raising various grounds.

5. Heard Mr. Abhijit Rathod, learned counsel appearing for the appellants, Ms. Pooja Choudhary,
learned Assistant Government Pleader, appearing for respondent No.1 and Mr. Rohan Lavkumar,
learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2 - Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam Ltd.
 
 C/FA/2675/2012 JUDGMENT DA

sentences.text: 6 . Learned counsel Mr. Rathod has submitted that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Reference Court is erroneous, unjust and inadequate and without appreciation of the evidence led before it.

He has submitted that the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge, Surendranagar had passed the Common Judgment in LAR Case Nos.251 of 2001 to 270 of 2001, 271 to 288 to 2001 & 289 of 2001 to 305 of 2001 dated 27.10.2009 in respect of the adjacent land of the present appellant of Mouje: Kherali, taluka: Wadhvan, District:
Surendranagar, whereby the compensation @ Rs.90/- for irrigated land was determined over and above the amount awarded as a compensation by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.

He has submitted that being aggrieved and dissatisfied by the aforesaid Common Judgment dated 27.10.2009, the Special Land Acquisition Officer had preferred Civil Application for condonation of delay No.10540 of 2012 in First Appeal (Stamp Number) No.2913 of 2012 to Civil Application No. 10594 of 2012 in First Appeal (Stamp Number) No.2697 of 2012 before this Court, whereby the delay condonation application was dismissed by the Division Bench of this Court by an order dated 09.01.2012 and thus, the award dated 27.10.2009 passed in respect of the adjacent land of Mouje Kherali, Taluka: Wadhvan, Dist. Surendranagar attained finality.

He has further submitted that against the LAR Case Nos.306 of 2001 with 307, 310 to 315, 317 to 319 & 322 of 2001, the Special Land Acquisition Officer had preferred First Appeal No.2791 of 2012 to 2807 of 2012 before this Court, wherein,
this Court (Coram: Hon'ble Mr. Justice K.M.Thaker) had passed an order dated 12.11.2016 in the Lok Adalat, whereby, the appeals came to be withdrawn by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.

sentences.text:
He has submitted that the Reference Court framed the issues below Exh. 12 and while deciding the same, so far as issue Nos.1 and 2 are NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2675/2012 JUDGMENT DATED:
03/10/2025 undefined concerned, the findings of the Reference Court are affirmative, however,
instead of granting the compensation @ Rs.90/- per sq. meter, the rate of Rs.30/- per sq. meter for non irrigated land and Rs.45/- per sq. meter for irrigated land has been awarded.
He has submitted that from the Form No.7/11 in connection with the land in question, it reveals that the land in question is adjacent to the agricultural land of village Kherali.
Village Ratanpar, Village: Kherali &

Village: Malod, which are nearby village of Tal. Wadhvan, Dist. Surendranagar and are within the distance of 7 kilometers, which fact has been admitted by the Special Land Acquisition Officer in his deposition recorded below Exh.78 in the examination in chief.

He has submitted that the Reference Court in the impugned award has recorded the findings that from the map at Exh.86, it is clear that village Malod is adjoining village of Kherali of Wadhvan Taluka and thus, the Reference Court ought to have considered the compensation awarded by the Judgment dated 27.10.2009 in LAR Case No.251 of 2001 & other allied References @ Rs.90/- per sq. meter in respect of the adjoining land of village Kherali, Tal. Wadhvan, Dist. Surendranagar.

He has submitted that the findings recorded by the Reference Court in the impugned award in para 24 is contrary to the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Shri Ambya Kalya Mhatre (D) Through Legal Heirs Nagarbhai Gangarambhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24694751/
4
Versus State Of Maharashtra reported in 2011 (9) SCC 325, more particularly, paragraphs 16 & 17.

He has submitted that the Expert Committee constituted by the Department for settlement of the proposal for Narmada Yojana under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, determined the compensation for the land situated at Mouje Malod, Tal. Wadhvan, Dist. Surendranagar in Compensation Case No.50 of 1999 and the land bearing Survey No.351 and amount of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2675/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/10/2025 undefined compensation of Rs. 103.50 paisa per sq. meter has been awarded to the land owners.

Learned counsel Mr. Rathod has, therefore,
urged that in view of the aforesaid facts, the impugned judgment and award be appropriately modified and the appeals be allowed to that extent.

7. Per contra, learned AGP Ms. Choudhary and learned counsel Mr. Rohan Lavkumar, appearing for the respective respondents, though have strongly objected the present appeals, however, on being enquired by the Court as to whether the order passed below Exh.-106 in LAR Case Nos.251 of 2001 to 270 of 2001, 271 to 288 to 2001 & 289 of 2001 to 305 of 2001 dated 27.10.2009 in respect of the adjacent land of the present appellant of Mouje: Kherali, taluka:
Wadhvan, District: Surendranagar, whereby the compensation @ Rs.90/- for irrigated land was determined, was challenged further before this Court by way of preferring any appeal or not, in response thereto, they have fairly admitted that they have accepted the award passed in case of village Kherali, Tal. Wadhwan, Dist.
Surendranagar and they have not challenged the same further and therefore,

8. I have heard the learned counsel appearing for the respective parties and perused the material placed on record.
I have also gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Reference Court.

The fact remains that the award passed by the Reference Court at Exh.-106 in case of village Kherali, Taluka: Wadhvan, District:
Surendranagar, whereby the additional compensation @ Rs.90/- was determined,
over and above the amount awarded by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, is accepted by the respondents and the said village Kherali is adjacent to the present village Malod.

I have also NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2675/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/10/2025 undefined considered the fact that the lands of present village Malod is just 13 kms. away from the Dist. Surendranagar and 7 kms. away from the city Wadhwan and there is approach road to the village and also having pre-primary,
primary and middle high school and also private hospital in the village and thus, all these indicate that village Malod is a developing village and naturally the acquired lands would having high potentiality.

Considering all these relevant factors and considering the submissions canvassed by both the sides, this Court is of the opinion that the appeals require consideration and the impugned judgment and award deserves to be modified to the extent that the appellants are entitled to get an additional amount of compensation at the rate of Rs.91.50ps. per square meter for non- irrigated lands and Rs.92/- per square meter for irrigated lands, taking into consideration the award passed at Exh.-106.

sentences.text: Resultantly, following final order is passed:-
All the first appeals are hereby allowed.

The appellants - claimants of these appeals shall be entitled to get additional amount of compensation at the rate of Rs.91.50ps.
per square meter for non- irrigated lands and Rs.92/- per square meter for irrigated lands, over and above the amount awarded by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.
The respondents shall deposit additional amount of compensation with statutory benefits before the Reference Court within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of the order.

On deposit of the amount, the same shall be disbursed in favour of each claimant, through RTGS / NEFT and the bank account details shall be furnished by the counsel for the claimants to the Registry of the Reference Court,
Surendranagar.
Other observations of the Reference Court for statutory benefits provided under the Act shall NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2675/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/10/2025 undefined remain intact.
Decree be drawn accordingly.
Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Reference Court forthwith.
10. In view of disposal of the First Appeals, the connected civil applications also stand disposed of accordingly.
